extracted.intended_audience: military administrators, Pay Department officials, Judge Advocates, and War Department legal officers handling desertion cases
extracted.subtask_description: Digest of War Department and judicial rules, precedents, and administrative practices governing desertion: restoration to duty, forfeitures, pardons, removal of charges, deserter's release, and related consequences for pay, citizenship, and property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration_to_duty_after_desertion
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier who deserted and reenlisted in another regiment may be restored to duty without trial in the second or fraudulent enlistment; there is no legal objection to such restoration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Soldier deserted and reenlisted; superior officers recommended pardon and restoration—held no legal objection to restoration without trial (C. 5465, Dec. 8, 1898).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration_on_surrender_and_command_application
rubrics_metrics.description: Where desertion arose from embarrassing conditions and the soldier surrenders seeking to return, he can be restored to duty without trial by proper authority, but application for such restoration should be made by a company commander.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Held where offender's only offense was desertion and he wished to return; restoration without trial permitted (C. 16306, May 7, 1904, et seq.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Making_good_time_lost
rubrics_metrics.description: Making good time lost by desertion is required (see forty-eighth article of war).

rubrics_metrics.name: No_pay_or_allowances_while_absent_for_desertion
rubrics_metrics.description: An enlisted man absent by reason of desertion is not rendering service under his enlistment contract and thus cannot acquire a right to pay or allowances during unauthorized absence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay and emoluments accrue only for service faithfully rendered; unauthorized absence bars accrual (C. 17768, Nov. 9, 1909; 27004, July 11, 1910).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disapproved_conviction_for_insufficient_evidence_no_forfeiture
rubrics_metrics.description: If a conviction for desertion is disapproved solely on the ground that the evidence does not sustain the charge, the soldier cannot legally be subjected to forfeiture of pay and allowances because he cannot be treated as a deserter in law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited authorities: R. 27.262 (Sept. 1868) and C. 17768 (Nov. 9, 1909).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture_requires_satisfactory_ascertainment_of_desertion
rubrics_metrics.description: Forfeiture of pay and allowances prescribed for deserters can be imposed only upon a satisfactory ascertainment of the fact of desertion; this may be established by court-martial or administratively in certain cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although a court-martial finding suffices, administrative establishment—e.g., restoration to duty without trial by competent authority—may also support forfeiture, but forfeiture generally applies only upon approved court-martial conviction (R. 7, 50, etc.; C. 4937; 7232).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharge_without_honor_as_evidence_for_withholding_pay
rubrics_metrics.description: An order directing discharge without honor on account of desertion is sufficient evidence to justify the Pay Department in withholding pay and allowances due at the time he was charged with desertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjutant_General_to_ascertain_status_for_pay_issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Where pay depends on status (absent with or without leave or desertion) the fact should be ascertained by The Adjutant General from his office records, who should report to the Paymaster General upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies when reviewing authority disapproves a finding without announcing reason (C. 17768, Nov. 9, 1909).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquittal_negates_forfeiture_even_if_disapproval_occurs
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier acquitted of desertion cannot be subjected to forfeiture of pay and allowances on account of desertion even though the finding be disapproved by the reviewing authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal_of_erroneous_charge_relieves_pay_stoppages
rubrics_metrics.description: If a soldier was erroneously charged on the rolls with desertion and the charge removed by War Department orders, the removal relieves him of any stoppages previously charged against his pay account on account of desertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities: R. 39, 41; C. 12227, Mar. 28 & Oct. 7, 1902; others. Removal operates as though no charge had been made. (See also footnote re: conditions when charge removed.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture_of_citizenship_only_on_approved_general_court-martial_conviction
rubrics_metrics.description: The forfeiture of rights of citizenship and incapacity to hold U.S. office imposed upon deserters by statute can be incurred only upon and incident to a conviction of desertion by a general court-martial, duly approved by competent authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These disabilities attach to every such conviction but may be removed by executive pardon; whether state voting rights are affected is determined by state law (numerous citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-citizen_deserter_not_forfeit_US_citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-citizen (e.g., a Filipino in the Philippine Scouts) who deserts does not forfeit U.S. citizenship (since not a U.S. citizen) and in absence of local law does not forfeit local citizenship either.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 23574, July 13, 1908. Applies where no congressional or commission law forfeiting local citizenship exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deserter_cannot_be_subjected_to_forfeiture_beyond_statute_or_regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: A deserter cannot legally be subjected to any forfeiture other than those prescribed by statute or Army regulation; private property and bounty monies are not forfeited by desertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: sale of private property to post fund unlawful; local bounty money already paid not forfeited; authorities R. 35, 13, 15, 16, 25. Private funds in care of company commander likewise not forfeited (J. 20812, Dec. 21, 1906).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharge_without_honor_while_insane_no_statutory_forfeitures
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a soldier was discharged without honor for desertion while in a Government hospital for the insane and circumstances indicate probable non-responsibility, he should not be visited with statutory forfeitures for desertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: G. 17327, Mar. 5, 1910. Applied when responsibility for acts is doubtful due to insanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture_of_paymaster_deposits_under_section_1305
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 1305, R.S., a soldier forfeited money he deposited with a paymaster on desertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture_of_amounts_after_settlement_for_company_indebtedness
rubrics_metrics.description: If a soldier who deserted owed money to the company fund, after his account is settled all moneys standing to his credit may be forfeited to the United States and cannot be set aside to pay his indebtedness to the company fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 14992, Aug. 28, 1903. Distinguishes deposits/credits vs private funds in possession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pardon_not_retroactive_and_does_not_remove_charge
rubrics_metrics.description: A pardon does not operate retroactively and cannot 'remove a charge' of desertion; it does not change the fact that the party deserted nor make the record say he did not desert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited authorities include R. 50, P. 42, P. 58, and numerous opinions (e.g., C. 1883, Aug. 8, 1896). Pardon cannot change historic facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential_proclamation_pardons_conditions_and_limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A Presidential proclamation (e.g., March 11, 1865) pardoning deserters who returned within specified time may impose conditions (serve remainder of original term plus additional time equal to time lost); failure to comply leaves charges standing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: deserter arrested during proclamation entitled to benefits; if failed to comply with service condition, charges allowed to stand (C. 1390, July 1895).

rubrics_metrics.name: No_general_amnesty_for_current_deserters
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no law extending amnesty to soldiers who are current deserters from the U.S. Army (i.e., no blanket amnesty then in force).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 778, Dec. 19, 1894. Department practice reflects this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department_will_not_consider_pardon_applications_of_fugitives
rubrics_metrics.description: The War Department has not considered applications for pardon of deserters who remain fugitives from justice; such applications are not entertained while the man is at large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many citations (C. 3304; 3656; 3950; etc.). Applicants generally must surrender or be in custody before consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration_to_duty_is_constructive_pardon
rubrics_metrics.description: Restoration to duty is treated as a constructive pardon for desertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 4076 (Apr. 30, 1898); C. 16814 (Sept. 3, 1904). Note distinction between removal of charge and the record of desertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice_of_securing_pardon_to_restore_citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: Department practice has been to seek a Presidential pardon to restore citizenship for soldiers convicted of desertion who served imposed imprisonment and whose subsequent civil conduct justifies a pardon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerous case citations show pardons obtained where conduct warranted restoration of citizenship (C. 14380, 14381, 14583, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pardon_applications_require_character_certificates_and_wait_period
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for pardon restoring citizenship lost under sections 1996 and 1998 R.S. should submit certificates from at least two reputable citizens as to reputation for honesty, industriousness, and moral character; applications generally considered only after one year since release from military control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice references: C. 19577-A with multiple dates (Aug.–Mar. series).

rubrics_metrics.name: Convicted_but_retained_in_service_must_apply_for_pardon_through_Adjutant_General
rubrics_metrics.description: If a general court-martial convicts a soldier of desertion but retains him in the service, he should be informed he must apply in a letter to The Adjutant General for a Presidential pardon to restore citizenship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary_of_War_may_determine_non-desertion_despite_discharge
rubrics_metrics.description: Although a legally executed discharge without honor cannot be set aside, on sufficient evidence the Secretary of War may decide that, notwithstanding the discharge for desertion, the man nevertheless was not a deserter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 8355; C. 12227; others. Secretary acts within discretion under relevant acts (e.g., Aug. 1, 1894).

rubrics_metrics.name: Desertion_and_honest_faithful_service_presumption_and_exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily desertion suffices to show service during that term was not honest and faithful, but in exceptional cases the Secretary of War may decide service was nevertheless honest and faithful under act of Aug. 1, 1894.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act of June 16, 1890 limited to certain purposes; citations: C. 2004, 2121, 3530, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honorable_discharge_removes_charge_for_that_enlistment
rubrics_metrics.description: A charge of desertion entered against a soldier in a particular term of enlistment is removed by an honorable discharge from that enlistment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 2041 (May 1896). Removal of charge as to that enlistment; factual record distinctions may remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction_of_rolls_when_later_proof_contrary
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it is subsequently established that a charged desertion was incorrect (e.g., soldier later found to have been a prisoner), the rolls should not be mutilated by erasure; subsequent rolls should enter the true facts and note the prior erroneous entry referring to the later roll.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insanity_at_time_of_desertion_supports_removal
rubrics_metrics.description: If a soldier was insane at the time of his desertion, the charge of desertion should be removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erroneous_drops_due_to_furlough_miscarriage_or_pass_accident_should_be_removed
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a soldier failed to receive notice due to mail miscarriage, or was unconscious from accident while on pass leading to drop as deserter, or was misinformed that furlough approved, the charge of desertion was erroneously made and should be removed; under such circumstances penal consequences should not follow and time lost need not be made good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 18352; C. 21117; C. 14398; C. 1A398. Specific facts determine removal; Army Regulations authorize departmental correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory_removal_of_charge_for_Civil_War_deserters_only
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of March 2, 1889 provides for removal of a charge of desertion only when the desertion occurred during the Civil War; persons whose cases had been judicially disposed of by trial/conviction/sentence are not within purview of statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 2683; R. 53, 143; C. 359 (Sept. 27, 1894). Removal of charge does not remove the fact of desertion from records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions_for_removal_under_act_of_Mar_2_1889_section_3
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3 of the act of March 2, 1889 allows removal of a charge of desertion only when three conditions are met: (1) soldier reenlisted within four months of desertion; (2) he faithfully served such reenlistment; and (3) such reenlistment was not made for the purpose of securing bounty, gratuity, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative cases where multiple reenlistments affected which charges could be removed (C. 3928; C. 23100; others). Even if charge removed, the record that he did not serve that earlier enlistment faithfully remains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlistment_elsewhere_to_secure_bounty_precludes_removal
rubrics_metrics.description: If subsequent enlistment was for the purpose of securing additional bounty/gratuity (e.g., enlisted to obtain $700 bounty total), removal of prior desertion charge is precluded under section 3 of March 2, 1889.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 14231 (Mar. 3, 1903). Facts about motives and bounty totals determine applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal_precluded_if_deserted_while_in_arrest_or_under_charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 7 of the act March 2, 1889 provides that the charge shall not be removed if the soldier left his command while in arrest or under charges for breach of military duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where soldier deserted while in arrest even if term had expired (C. 3099, Apr. 12, 1897).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafted_men_who_failed_to_report_not_within_act_meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: A drafted man declared 'a deserter' for failing to report to enrollment board had only limited military status; prior to acceptance/rejection by the board he was not fully in military service and therefore not within meaning of act allowing removal—charge could not be removed under that act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 2041, 2042 (May 1896). Distinguishes drafted status vs full enlistment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act_of_May_17_1886_removal_if_enlisted_within_three_months
rubrics_metrics.description: Act of May 17, 1886 provided that where a Civil War soldier deserted from one organization and within three months enlisted in another, the charge could be removed and a certificate of discharge issued from the organization in which he first served, changing his status to honorably discharged as of the date of desertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 2090 (Mar. 1896). Legislative purpose: alter beneficiary status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration_without_trial_does_not_remove_charge
rubrics_metrics.description: Restoration to duty without trial does not operate as an acquittal nor remove the charge of desertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 4076; C. 18678; C. 14398; upheld that restoration is not an acquittal though treated as constructive pardon in some contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquittal_by_regimental_court_without_jurisdiction_does_not_remove_charge
rubrics_metrics.description: An acquittal by a regimental court-martial that lacks jurisdiction does not operate to remove the charge of desertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 995 (Feb. 15, 1895); C. 27004 (July 11, 1910). Jurisdictional defects leave charge intact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deserter_release_purpose_and_eligibility_period
rubrics_metrics.description: The deserter's release (General Orders 55 of 1890) is intended for deserters whose one hundred and third article of war limitation has fully run; release is afforded when two years from end of term of enlistment have elapsed (exclusive of absences from U.S.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities: P. 52, 61, 62, 63; C. 96; O. 4130; C. 14163; C. 15257. If arrested/convicted before that period, release cannot be accorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deserter_release_not_for_dishonorably_discharged_or_mustered_out_volunteers
rubrics_metrics.description: A person dishonorably discharged or a soldier of a volunteer organization mustered out is not within the class intended for a deserter's release; the release is for soldiers actually in service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P. 63; C. 15460; other citations. Release cannot be issued to deceased persons either.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deserter_release_not_equivalent_to_discharge_certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The deserter's release relieves from liability to arrest and trial but does not serve as a discharge from the Army, is not evidence of discharge, and should be prepared so as to preclude any claim that it operates as an actual discharge certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P. 52, 61, 62, 63; Circular No. 5, A. G. O., 1894; C. 13896; C. 21367. Language in General Orders describing it as 'Release from the Army' is faulty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure_to_secure_deserter_release
rubrics_metrics.description: To secure a deserter's release the deserter should surrender to military authorities nearest his residence and apply to The Adjutant General with an affidavit that he has remained constantly in the United States since desertion, supported by such affidavits as he can obtain; upon establishment of facts a release issues as a matter of course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 14163 (July 11, 1911). Indicates practical procedural steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time_of_war_determination_for_desertion
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a desertion occurred 'in time of war' depends on date relative to exchange of ratification and, where theater of operations is abroad, the U.S. is considered in time of war at home as well as abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 15417; C. 16064; C. 4050 (Apr. 23, 1898). Example: desertion on Oct. 25, 1898 prior to exchange of ratification held to be in time of war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility_for_Government_property_lost_due_to_desertion
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier responsible for Government property who deserts and causes disappearance of the property remains responsible for the loss even if acquitted of stealing; acquittal of theft does not relieve responsibility as loss may be attributed to desertion by a board of survey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 721 (Dec. 1894). Civil and administrative liability distinguished from criminal acquittal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officers_absconding_with_Government_funds_or_false_pretexts_may_be_charged_with_desertion
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer who absconds while on leave and does not return, especially when accompanied by misappropriation of Government funds or obtaining leave by false representations and traveling to remote localities, may be properly charged with desertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases: R. 3, 230 (July 1863); R. 38, 622 (June 1877). The circumstances and presumption of intent to desert govern chargeability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects_of_deserted_commissioned_officer_regarded_as_abandoned
rubrics_metrics.description: The effects (personal property) of a commissioned officer who deserts will be collected the same as those of an enlisted man and regarded as abandoned and so treated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 17191 (Dec. 19, 1904). Distinguishes treatment of property irrespective of rank.
